extension.summary: Up to eight colours of particles, random rules or classic presets, and the patterns that follow
extension.description:
A Kodi screensaver port of the openFrameworks Particle Life app. Colours of particles attract and repel each other under a matrix of pair forces, and out of those rules come cells, chains, membranes, orbiting clusters and drifting colonies. The rules are re-rolled on a timer (60 seconds by default) so the pattern never settles into one look.
The rules can be random (one to eight colours, optionally symmetric, with a random number of colours and a random viscosity for each set) or come from the 19 saved models that ship with the original app, such as Worm, Flower cell, DNA, Ladybug and Soap, shown in order, shuffled, mixed with random rules, or one of them on its own. "Evolve" slowly drifts every rule, "random exploration" flips one rule at a time as in the JavaScript version, and random pulses now and then blow the particles apart or pull them together.
Everything is configured in the add-on settings rather than an in-app panel: particles per colour, simulation steps per second, re-roll interval, rule source, colours, viscosity and friction, force strength, interaction range, gravity, wall repulsion and hard bounds, plus the look: Classic, Neon, Pastel, Rainbow or random-hue palettes, round, square or glowing particles, particle size and motion trails. The simulation is CPU-side with a uniform neighbour grid, so 4,000 particles cost about 2 ms a step on a desktop, and the particles are drawn as a single stream of point sprites with plain OpenGL 2 / OpenGL ES 2. The simulation runs in a 900-pixel-high space that widens with the screen, so the force radii keep the original's scale on any display.
extension.disclaimer: This is a native add-on: it is built per platform and Kodi version (this one: Kodi 21 Omega on macOS, Intel and Apple Silicon, and 64-bit Android). It needs OpenGL or OpenGL ES 2.0. Particle Life was created by Hunar Ahmad (https://github.com/hunar4321/life_code, MIT); this is an independent native port of the same idea with its own simulation, renderer and settings.
extension.news: 1.1.0 - the 19 saved models from the original app as presets (in order, shuffled, mixed with random rules, or one fixed preset); 1 to 8 colours with Classic, Neon, Pastel, Rainbow and random-hue palettes; symmetric rules, random exploration, random colour counts and viscosity per rule set, random pulses and gravity; round, square and glow particles; motion trails. 1.0.0 - initial release
